signature: question -> card: str, reward_inr: float, reply: str  # instructions: Pick the best credit card for the purchase. Use the tools. Only use numbers that come from tool results.

tools.name: classify_merchant
tools.doc:
Look up the spending category of a merchant name, e.g. "Amazon" -> "amazon".

Returns one of the known category names, or a string starting with "error:" if the merchant is unknown.

tools.name: rank_cards
tools.doc:
Rank all credit cards for a purchase, best first.

Args:
    amount: purchase amount in rupees, greater than 0.
    category: a category returned by classify_merchant.

Returns a list of {"card": card id, "rate_pct": reward rate in percent, "reward_inr": rupees earned},
best reward first, ties broken by card id. Returns an error string for a bad amount or category.

tools.name: submit
tools.doc: Submit the final outputs for the task.

note: This is DSPy's real prompt format, generated with a recording fake model (dspy.utils.DummyLM); no optimizer was run against our 1.5B model. Our live agent does not use this prompt (it uses the shorter prompt in agent-step.js) unless a later change measures it. Target question is C01; few-shot demos come from C02, C03, C04 with reply sentences written from their expected values. DSPy 3.5.0 ReAct has no separate extract step: it calls a built-in submit tool, so the zero-shot variant also carries secondTurnMessages (after one tool result) and finalTurnMessages (the submit turn). Few-shot variant is dspy.Predict with LabeledFewShot over the same signature. LabeledFewShot on dspy.ReAct ran, but its prompt came out identical to zero-shot: the demos (question, card, reward_inr, reply) do not match ReAct's inner signature (next_thought, tool_calls), so DSPy dropped them. The Predict variant has no tools, so its instruction sentence mentions tools that it cannot call.
